questions.content:
Mount Ardent is an active composite volcano near the town of Halvern. After a series of small eruptions, the authorities divided the area around the crater into three hazard zones.

Zone | Distance from crater (km) | People living in zone
Red | 0 - 5 | 4,000
Orange | 5 - 10 | 18,000
Yellow | 10 - 20 | 60,000

(a) Calculate the total number of people living within 10 km of the crater. (1 mark)
(b) Calculate the percentage of all the people living within 20 km of the crater who live in the Yellow zone. Show your working and give your answer to one decimal place. (2 marks)
(c) Explain one way that monitoring a volcano can reduce the number of deaths when it erupts. (2 marks)
questions.mark_scheme:
[1] (a) 4,000 + 18,000 = 22,000 people.
[1] (b) Correct working: 60,000 / (4,000 + 18,000 + 60,000) x 100 = 60,000 / 82,000 x 100.
[1] (b) Answer 73.2% (accept 73%).
[1] (c) Identifies a valid monitoring method, e.g. seismometers detecting small earthquakes, measuring gas emissions, ground tilt or swelling, or temperature changes.
[1] (c) Explains how it saves lives, e.g. changes give early warning so people can be evacuated before the eruption and emergency services can prepare.
Accept other valid points.

questions.content:
The Tarun region contains a large tropical rainforest. Satellite images were used to measure how much forest remained at three dates.

Year | Forest cover (square km)
2000 | 8,400
2010 | 7,140
2020 | 5,712

A group of students wants to investigate how clearing forest affects soil erosion on hillsides in the region. They plan to compare a forested hillside with a hillside that has been cleared for farming.

(a) Calculate the percentage decrease in forest cover between 2000 and 2020. Show your working. (2 marks)
(b) Calculate the mean loss of forest per year between 2010 and 2020. (1 mark)
(c) Suggest one suitable method for collecting primary data about soil erosion on each hillside. (1 mark)
(d) Explain why the students should measure the same slope angle and rainfall conditions at both hillsides. (2 marks)
questions.mark_scheme:
[1] (a) Working: (8,400 - 5,712) / 8,400 x 100.
[1] (a) Answer 32% (a decrease of 32.0%).
[1] (b) (7,140 - 5,712) / 10 = 142.8 square km per year.
[1] (c) A valid method, e.g. erosion pins measured over time, measuring depth of exposed roots or topsoil, collecting runoff in a bottle and measuring sediment, or a turbidity reading of streams.
[1] (d) To make it a fair test, only the vegetation cover should differ between the hillsides (control other variables).
[1] (d) Slope angle and rainfall also affect erosion, so if they differed the students could not tell whether deforestation caused the difference in results.
Accept other valid points.

questions.content:
Isla Corvo is a small tropical island whose economy relies on tourism. Most hotels are owned by international companies and most food and equipment is imported.

Year | Tourist arrivals (thousands) | Average spending per tourist (US dollars)
2015 | 120 | 900
2023 | 210 | 1,100

It is estimated that 55% of the money spent by tourists leaves the island.

(a) Calculate the total spending by tourists in 2023, in millions of US dollars. Show your working. (2 marks)
(b) Calculate the percentage increase in tourist arrivals between 2015 and 2023. (1 mark)
(c) Define the term leakage in tourism. (1 mark)
(d) Calculate how much of the 2023 tourist spending stays on Isla Corvo, in millions of US dollars. (1 mark)
(e) State one negative environmental impact of a large increase in tourist numbers on a coral reef coast. (1 mark)
questions.mark_scheme:
[1] (a) Working: 210,000 x 1,100.
[1] (a) Answer 231 million dollars.
[1] (b) (210 - 120) / 120 x 100 = 75%.
[1] (c) Money spent by tourists that leaves the local economy, e.g. profits sent abroad by foreign owners or payments for imports.
[1] (d) 45% of 231 = 103.95 million dollars (accept about 104 million).
[1] (e) A valid impact, e.g. coral damaged by boat anchors, snorkelling or divers touching it, pollution from sewage, or sunscreen chemicals harming the reef.
Accept other valid points.

questions.content:
Tropical storm Hurana formed over the warm ocean and moved towards the coast of the country of Valdoro. The table shows the maximum wind speed recorded on the day it approached land.

Time | Maximum wind speed (km per hour)
00:00 | 90
06:00 | 120
12:00 | 165
18:00 | 150

Use clear geographical terms in your answers.

(a) State two conditions needed for a tropical storm to form. (2 marks)
(b) Calculate the percentage increase in maximum wind speed between 00:00 and 12:00. Give your answer to one decimal place. (2 marks)
(c) Explain how a storm surge can cause flooding on the coast. (2 marks)
questions.mark_scheme:
[1] (a) First valid condition, e.g. sea surface temperature of at least 27 degrees Celsius, or ocean water warm to a depth of about 50 m.
[1] (a) Second different condition, e.g. located about 5 to 30 degrees north or south of the equator (so the Coriolis effect can make the storm spin), or low wind shear, or a pre-existing area of low pressure.
[1] (b) Working: (165 - 90) / 90 x 100.
[1] (b) Answer 83.3%.
[1] (c) The very low pressure at the centre of the storm and the strong onshore winds raise the sea level and push a mass of water towards the coast.
[1] (c) The raised water, together with high tides and waves, flows over low-lying land and defences, flooding homes and farmland.
Accept other valid points.

questions.content:
Dalmar is a country that relies on rice as its main food. The table shows national rice production and population.

Year | Rice production (million tonnes) | Population (millions)
2010 | 3.0 | 12
2020 | 3.6 | 16

1 tonne = 1,000 kg.

(a) Calculate the amount of rice produced per person in 2010, in kilograms. Show your working. (2 marks)
(b) Calculate the amount of rice produced per person in 2020, in kilograms. (1 mark)
(c) Calculate the percentage change in rice produced per person between 2010 and 2020. (1 mark)
(d) Explain one reason why many people in a country can still be food insecure even when total food production rises. (2 marks)
questions.mark_scheme:
[1] (a) Working: 3,000,000 tonnes x 1,000 / 12,000,000 people (or 3.0 / 12 = 0.25 tonnes).
[1] (a) Answer 250 kg per person.
[1] (b) 3.6 million tonnes / 16 million = 225 kg per person.
[1] (c) (225 - 250) / 250 x 100 = -10% (a decrease of 10%).
[1] (d) Identifies a valid reason, e.g. population growth is faster than production growth, poverty means people cannot afford food, poor roads and storage prevent distribution, or crops are exported or wasted.
[1] (d) Explains the link, e.g. the food produced is shared between more people or cannot reach those who need it, so some households still go hungry.
Accept other valid points.

questions.content:
Zentrix Electronics, a transnational corporation (TNC) with its headquarters in the high-income country of Harland, opened a large factory in the low-income country of Lumeria.

Factory worker monthly wage in Harland: 2,600 US dollars
Factory worker monthly wage in the Zentrix factory in Lumeria: 380 US dollars
Average monthly wage in Lumeria: 290 US dollars
Jobs created in the Lumeria factory: 5,000
Share of components bought from Lumerian suppliers: 12%
Share of profits sent back to Harland: 85%

(a) Calculate how many times greater the monthly factory wage in Harland is than in the Zentrix factory in Lumeria. Give your answer to one decimal place. (2 marks)
(b) State one way that improved communications technology has helped the growth of TNCs. (1 mark)
(c) Analyse the impacts of the Zentrix factory on Lumeria. Use evidence from the information above. (4 marks)
questions.mark_scheme:
[1] (a) Working: 2,600 / 380.
[1] (a) Answer 6.8.
[1] (b) A valid way, e.g. the internet and video links allow head offices to manage distant factories, or fast data transfer allows supply chains to be coordinated across countries.
[1] (c) Positive economic impact with data: 5,000 jobs created and pay (380 dollars) about 31% above the national average of 290 dollars.
[1] (c) Limited benefit to the wider economy: only 12% of components come from local suppliers, so few other businesses gain and the multiplier effect is small.
[1] (c) Much of the wealth leaves: 85% of profits go back to Harland, so Lumeria keeps little of the income produced.
[1] (c) Balanced judgement, e.g. workers are paid far less than in Harland (about 15% of the Harland wage), which may be exploitation, although the jobs may bring skills and technology transfer.
Accept other valid points.

questions.content:
Pellin Sands is a seaside town of 3,500 people on a soft clay coastline. The cliff is eroding at an average of 1.8 m per year and sea level is rising. In the next 40 years, 640 properties are at risk. Of these, 210 properties are within 72 m of the cliff edge. The town council can afford only one of the following plans.

Option 1: Sea wall along 2 km of coast
Construction cost: 18 million dollars
Maintenance: 0.3 million dollars per year
Lifespan: 40 years
Properties protected: all 640 
Other effects: protects the beach tourism businesses in the short term, but waves reflected by the wall are expected to remove most of the sand in front of it

Option 2: Managed retreat
Cost: 11 million dollars to buy and relocate 210 properties
Monitoring: 0.05 million dollars per year
Other effects: 25 hectares of salt marsh would be created to absorb wave energy, protecting the other 430 properties; 210 households would lose their homes and would have to move inland

(a) Calculate the total cost of each option over 40 years (construction or purchase cost plus maintenance or monitoring). Show your working. (2 marks)
(b) Evaluate which option would be the better way to manage the coastline at Pellin Sands. Support your answer with evidence from the information and reach a justified conclusion. (7 marks)
questions.mark_scheme:
[1] (a) Option 1: 18 + (0.3 x 40) = 30 million dollars.
[1] (a) Option 2: 11 + (0.05 x 40) = 13 million dollars.
[1] (b) Option 1 benefit with data: protects all 640 properties and the town's beach tourism businesses.
[1] (b) Option 1 cost: 30 million dollars is more than twice the cost of Option 2 (about 2.3 times) and the wall only lasts 40 years, after which it would need replacing.
[1] (b) Option 1 environmental or long-term drawback: reflected waves remove sand, so the beach (and the tourism it supports) may be lost; sea walls do not work with natural processes.
[1] (b) Option 2 benefit: cheaper (13 million dollars), creates 25 hectares of salt marsh habitat and absorbs wave energy naturally, making it more sustainable.
[1] (b) Option 2 drawback: 210 households lose their homes and communities, causing social and emotional harm and possible disputes over compensation; the remaining 430 properties depend on the marsh working as expected.
[1] (b) Evaluative weighing, e.g. short-term protection of homes and income against long-term cost, environment and fairness, or noting that erosion of 1.8 m per year (72 m in 40 years) and sea level rise will continue regardless.
[1] (b) Clear conclusion consistent with the evidence, with a justification and recognition of one condition or uncertainty (e.g. adequate compensation, whether the salt marsh will be effective).
Accept other valid points.
